blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to empower models to continuously acquire new knowledge while mitigating catastrophic forgetting. With the advent of vision-language models like CLIP, leveraging their cross-modal alignment capabilities to address CIL challenges has emerged as a dominant paradigm. Existing methods leverage CLIP's global representations (i.e., the visual [CLS] token and the textual [EOS] token) for cross-modal alignment. While achieving effective classification, they overlook the rich patch-level visual features and token-level textual semantics inherent in CLIP. For example, the [CLS] token aggregates local information to capture the general concept of "cat", while the patch-level details retain specific localized features essential for recognition, such as the tail, fur, and face. We propose PACE (PAtch-token Cross-modal Enhancement) to uncover the long-neglected local representations within CLIP. First, based on the global representations like [CLS] token and [EOS] token, we identify the top-k most crucial visual patches and textual tokens. Subsequently, to better utilize the extracted key local features, we design a cross-modal fusion module. This module leverages local textual semantics to refine visual representations, while augmenting textual semantics with local visual features. As the fusion module is shared across all tasks, directly fine-tuning it on new tasks would interfere with the knowledge learned from previous tasks, leading to catastrophic forgetting. To alleviate this, we employ a projection-based update strategy to effectively preserve the critical parameter space of previous tasks during the adaptation to new tasks. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PACE significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods across multiple CIL benchmarks.
blocks.zh: 班级强化学习(CIL)旨在增强模型的能力,以不断获得新知识,同时减轻灾难性的遗忘. 随着像CLIP这样的愿景语言模式的出现,利用其跨模式的对接能力来应对CIL挑战已成为主导范例. 现有方法利用CLIP的全球表示(即视觉[CLS]符号和文字[EOS]符号)来进行跨模式对接. 在实现有效分类的同时,它们忽略了CLIP中固有的丰富的补丁级视觉特征和符号级文字语义. 例如,[CLS]令牌汇总了本地信息来捕捉"猫"的一般概念,而补丁级细节则保留了识别所必需的特定局部特征,如尾巴,毛皮,和相貌等. 我们建议PACE(Patch-token Cross-Model-Administration)在CLIP中找出长期被忽视的地方代表. 首先,根据全球的表示,如[CLS]符和[EOS]符,我们确定最关键的视觉补丁和文字符. 之后,为了更好地利用提取出的关键局部特征,我们设计出一个跨模式聚变模块. 这个模块利用了本地文字语义来完善视觉表现,同时用本地视觉特征来扩充文字语义. 由于聚变模块是在所有任务中共享的,直接调整其新任务会干扰从以前任务中获取的知识,导致灾难性的遗忘. 为了缓解这种情况,我们采用了基于预测的更新战略,以有效保留适应新任务期间以往任务的关键参数空间。 广泛的实验表明,PACE在多种CIL基准方面大大超过最先进的方法。

blocks.en: I Introduction
blocks.zh: 一. 导言

blocks.en: In recent years, the rapid advancement of deep learning [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] has exerted a profound influence across numerous fields, demonstrating significant advantages and potential. However, real-world scenarios are inherently dynamic. Data typically emerges as continuous, evolving data streams [ 4 , 5 ] , posing substantial challenges for traditional deep learning models. To address this challenge, Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) [ 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 ] has been proposed as a new research paradigm, enabling models to incrementally absorb new knowledge. A primary obstacle for CIL is catastrophic forgetting [ 10 ] , [ 11 ] , in which the model tends to fit current data while forgetting previously acquired knowledge. With the rapid development of Pre-trained Models (PTMs) [ 12 ] , [ 13 ] , such as Vision Transformers [ 14 ] and CLIP [ 15 ] , leveraging their inherent generalization capabilities has become a dominant trend [ 16 , 17 ] . Consequently, current CIL [ 18 ] research has shifted from traditional training from scratch with randomly initialized weights to utilizing existing PTMs, which require training only a small number of additional parameters [ 19 , 20 , 21 ] .
blocks.zh: 近年来,深入学习的迅速发展[1,2,3]在许多领域产生了深刻的影响,显示出巨大的优势和潜力. 然而,现实世界的情景本身是动态的。 数据通常作为持续、不断发展的数据流[4、5]出现,对传统的深入学习模式构成重大挑战。 为了应对这一挑战,提出了班级强化学习(CIL)[6,7,8,9]作为一个新的研究范式,使模型能够逐渐吸收新的知识. CIL的一个主要障碍是灾难性地忘记[10],[11],其中模型倾向于适应当前数据而忘记以前获得的知识. 随着训练前模型(PTMs)[12],[13]的迅速发展,例如Vision Transformers[14]和CLIP[15],利用它们固有的通俗化能力成为主流趋势[16,17]. 因此,目前的CIL[18]研究已经从零开始随机初始加权的传统培训转向利用现有的PTM,这仅需要培训少量额外参数[19、20、21]。

blocks.en: CLIP [ 15 ] , as a pioneering pre-trained vision-language model [ 22 ] , maps images and texts into a shared embedding space via contrastive learning, effectively achieving cross-modal alignment with powerful zero-shot generalization and semantic representation capabilities. Specifically, the image encoder of CLIP prepends a learnable [CLS] token to the input sequence of image patches to aggregate global visual features, while the text encoder utilizes the [EOS] token at the end of the sequence to summarize the overall textual semantics. Although both encoders simultaneously output a sequence of patch-tokens containing rich spatial details [ 23 ] , [ 24 ] and a sequence of word-tokens carrying local semantics during processing, CLIP’s cross-modal matching mechanism relies solely on computing the cosine similarity between the global embeddings. While this design achieves efficient global alignment, it inherently disregards the local feature sequences that harbor specific details during the final matching stage [ 25 ] . For instance, when distinguishing between a “ sparrow ” and a “ robin ”, the image explicitly contains a clear “beak” patch. However, since the matching process relies solely on holistic semantic features, these critical local details cannot be effectively utilized during mapping.
blocks.zh: CLIP [15],作为一个先行的预训视觉语言模型[22],通过对比性学习将图像和文本映射到共享嵌入空间中,有效实现与强大的零镜头概括和语义表现能力的跨模式对齐. 具体地说,CLIP的图像编码器预先将一个可学习的[CLS]符号插入到图像补丁的输入序列中,以聚合全局视觉特征,而文本编码器则利用序列末端的[EOS]符号来概括整个文字语义. 虽然两个编码器同时输出一个包含丰富空间细节的补丁键序列[23],[24]和处理过程中带局部语义的单词键序列,但CLIP的跨模式匹配机制完全依赖于计算全球嵌入体之间的余弦相似性. 虽然这种设计实现了高效的全球对齐,但本质上忽略了在最终匹配阶段隐藏具体细节的局部特征序列[25]. 例如,在区分“麻雀”和“robin”时,图像明确包含一个明显的“喙”补丁。 然而,由于配对过程完全依赖于整体语义特征,这些关键的局部细节在绘图过程中无法有效利用.

blocks.en: Recent studies [ 26 ] , [ 27 ] in CIL have focused on Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) strategies, such as prompt learning [ 28 ] , [ 29 ] and adapter tuning [ 30 ] , [ 31 ] to mitigate catastrophic forgetting. Despite their effectiveness in balancing stability and plasticity, these methods largely inherit the global alignment paradigm of the original CLIP. Specifically, existing works focus on optimizing learnable prompts or refining global [CLS] and [EOS] representations. Consequently, they also overlook the discriminative potential of both visual patch-tokens and textual tokens, leaving the rich local spatial features and local semantic contexts, which are crucial for class-incremental learning.
blocks.zh: 近期在CIL的研究[26],[27]集中研究了参数-有效精细图解(PEFT)策略,如即时学习[28],[29]和适配器调制[30],[31]以减轻灾难性的遗忘. 尽管这些方法在平衡稳定性和可塑性方面是有效的,但它们在很大程度上继承了最初的CLIP的全球对齐范式. 具体而言,现有工作的重点是优化可学习的提示或改进全球[CLS]和[EOS]表述。 因此,它们也忽略了视觉补丁和文字符号的歧视性潜力,留下了丰富的当地空间特征和地方语义背景,而这些特征和背景对班级的强化学习至关重要。

blocks.en: Leveraging the local information carried by patch-tokens offers a promising approach to enhancing CLIP’s discriminative capabilities in class-incremental learning. However, two major challenges remain: 1) Acquiring and effectively utilizing local information. Although both the visual and text encoders of CLIP output rich local features, this information is not effectively utilized by the existing matching mechanism. Furthermore, since image patches contain substantial redundant noise, and the text includes non-informative stop words. So we need to select discriminative local features and design a novel matching paradigm that enables the effective utilization of patch-tokens to jointly contribute to the classification decision. 2) Mitigating forgetting when utilizing local knowledge. As class-incremental learning involves continuous updates to the data stream, the model risks forgetting previously acquired knowledge after each update. Therefore, it is crucial to retain learned local knowledge effectively and mitigate catastrophic forgetting throughout the updating process.
blocks.zh: 利用补丁所携带的当地信息,为增强CLIP在班级递增学习中的歧视性能力提供了一个很有希望的办法。 然而,仍然存在两大挑战: (1) 获取和有效利用当地信息。 虽然CLIP的视觉和文本编码器都输出了丰富的本地特性,但现有的匹配机制并没有有效地利用这些信息. 此外,由于图像补丁包含大量的冗余噪声,文本中包含非信息性停止词. 因此,我们需要选择带有歧视性的地方特征,并设计一个新的匹配范式,以便有效地利用补丁键来共同促进分类决定。 (2) 在利用当地知识时减轻遗忘。 由于班级增量学习涉及数据流的不断更新,模型在每次更新后都有可能忘记以前获得的知识. 因此,在更新过程中有效保留当地知识并减轻灾难性的遗忘至关重要。

blocks.en: To address these challenges, we propose PACE (PAtch-token Cross-modal Enhancement) for CLIP-based CIL. First, we address the critical issue of the availability of local features. We uncover the long-neglected local representations within CLIP, extracting the crucial top- k k patch-level visual features and token-level textual semantics essential for discrimination, and map them into their respective modal shared spaces. Subsequently, to fully leverage these key local elements, we design a cross-modal fusion module. Token-level textual semantics are utilized to refine the global image representation, while patch-level visual features are simultaneously injected into the text embeddings to enhance their semantic specificity. Finally, the global shared weights of the cross-modal fusion module are highly susceptible to destructive gradient updates from new tasks. To prevent catastrophic forgetting during updates, we adopt a projection-based parameter update strategy. This mechanism effectively preserves the critical parameter space associated with previously acquired knowledge. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance, demonstrating significant improvements across all nine benchmark datasets.
blocks.zh: 为了应对这些挑战,我们提议为基于CLIP的CIL提供PACE(Patch-token Cross-modle-Information). 第一,我们处理具有当地特点的关键问题。 我们揭开长期忽略的CLIP内部的本地表述, 提取对歧视至关重要的顶级- k 补丁级视觉特征和象征级文字语义, 随后,为了充分利用这些关键的局部元素,我们设计了一个跨模式聚变模块. 托肯级文字语义被用于完善全局图像表达,而补丁级视觉特征则同时注入文字嵌入,以加强其语义特性. 最后,跨模式聚变模块的全球共享权重极易受到新任务的破坏性梯度更新. 为防止在更新过程中发生灾难性的遗忘,我们采取了基于预测的参数更新策略. 这一机制有效地保留了与先前获得的知识相关的关键参数空间。 我们的方法实现了最先进的性能,显示出所有9个基准数据集的重大改进。

blocks.en: II Related Work
blocks.zh: 二. 相关工作

blocks.en: II-A Class-Incremental Learning
blocks.zh: II-A级强化学习

blocks.en: Class-Incremental Learning aims to continuously acquire knowledge from new tasks while preventing catastrophic forgetting [ 32 ] , [ 33 ] . Typical CIL methods can be broadly categorized into several distinct groups. Replay-based methods [ 34 ] , [ 35 ] mitigate forgetting by maintaining a small memory buffer to store representative exemplars of old classes, which are then replayed during the training of new tasks [ 36 ] , [ 37 ] . Model rectification-based methods rectify the inductive biases within the model, such as classifier weights [ 38 ] , [ 39 ] and biased logits [ 40 ] . Dynamic network-based methods [ 41 ] , [ 42 ] dynamically adjust or expand the network structure during the incremental process to better accommodate new classes, typically involving neuron expansion [ 43 ] , backbone expansion [ 44 ] , and prompt expansion [ 45 ] . Knowledge distillation-based methods [ 4 ] , [ 46 ] leverage distillation techniques to transfer knowledge from the old model to the current one, constraining the model to balance between learning new tasks while retaining old ones [ 47 ] , [ 48 ] . Regularization-based methods impose constraints on critical parameters, minimize their deviation, and thus resist forgetting [ 49 ] , [ 50 ] .
blocks.zh: 职等递增 学习的目的是不断从新任务中获得知识,同时防止灾难性的遗忘[32]、[33]。 典型的CIL方法可以大致分为几个不同的组别. 基于重播的方法 [34], [35] 通过维持一个小的内存缓冲器来存储旧班级的代表性实例来缓解遗忘,然后在训练新任务时重播 [36], [37]. 基于模型的纠正方法纠正了模型中的诱导偏差,如分类器权重[38],[39]和偏差对数[40]. 基于网络的动态方法[41],[42]在增量过程中动态调整或扩大网络结构,以更好地适应新的类别,一般涉及神经元扩张[43],骨干扩张[44],以及迅速扩展[45]. 基于知识的蒸馏方法[4],[46] 利用蒸馏技术将知识从旧模型转移到目前的模型,制约模型在学习新任务和保留旧任务之间取得平衡[47],[48]. 基于规范化的方法对关键参数施加限制,尽量减少其偏差,从而避免忘记[49],[50].

blocks.en: II-B Pre-Trained Model-Based CIL
blocks.zh: II-B 培训前模式CIL

blocks.en: The advent of powerful Pre-trained Models (PTMs), such as ViT [ 14 ] and CLIP [ 15 ] , has precipitated a paradigm shift in CIL, moving from training models from scratch with randomly initialized weights to harnessing pre-trained foundations [ 7 ] . To preserve the pre-trained knowledge, a common strategy is to freeze the PTM backbone and add lightweight, learnable modules for adaptation [ 51 ] , [ 52 ] . For example, Prompt-based methods ( e.g. , L2P [ 53 ] , DualPrompt [ 54 ] ) design a visual prompt pool [ 55 ] that utilizes learnable prompts to encode task-specific information into the input sequence of the frozen backbone. Recent work has further optimized the dynamic adaptability of prompt generation by introducing mechanisms such as attention modules [ 51 ] and generative networks [ 56 ] . Adapter-based methods [ 30 ] , [ 57 ] , on the other hand, achieve adaptation by inserting lightweight modules into the frozen network layers. Building upon this foundation, a prominent trend has emerged that leverages the robust cross-modal alignment capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs), such as CLIP. Specifically, PROOF [ 20 ] augments CLIP’s representational capacity by appending novel projection layers. RAPF [ 58 ] introduces a strategy for adaptive representation adjustment and decomposed parameter fusion. By decomposing parameters into shared and task-specific components via weighted fusion, this method effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting. Furthermore, CLG-CBM [ 59 ] incorporates language-guided concept bottleneck models. To maintain semantic consistency across tasks, these models align visual features into a human-interpretable concept space. MG-CLIP [ 27 ] introduces modality gap preservation and compensation to mitigate forgetting and improve adaptation to new tasks, while HERMAN [ 60 ] proposes hierarchical representation matching for CLIP-based CIL. However, existing CLIP-based CIL methods still primarily rely on global representations for incremental recognition, leaving the patch-level visual features and token-level textual semantics within CLIP insufficiently explored. This paper aims to explore the long-neglected local representations within CLIP for improving incremental recognition in CLIP-based CIL.
blocks.zh: 强大的训练前模型(PTM)的出现,如VIT[14]和CLIP[15],促使CIL的范式转变,从随机初始加权的训练模式从零开始,转向利用训练前的基础[7]. 为了保存经过预先训练的知识,一个共同的战略是冻结PTM主干线,并增加轻量级,可学习的适应模块[51],[52]. 例如,即时方法(例如,L2P [53],DualPrompt [54])设计了一个可视化的即时集合[55],利用可学习的即时将特定任务信息编码到被冻结的主干线的输入序列中. 最近的工作通过引入关注模块[51]和基因网络[56]等机制,进一步优化了迅速生成的动态适应性. 而基于适配器的方法[30],[57]则通过在冷冻的网络层中插入轻量级模块来实现适配. 在这一基础上,出现了一种突出的趋势,利用了Visual-Langage Models(VLMs)强有力的跨模式对接能力,例如CLIP。 具体来说,PROOF[20]通过附加新的投影层来增强CLIP的代表能力. RAPF[58]引入了适应性代表调整和分解参数聚变的战略. 通过加权聚变将参数分解成共同的和特定任务的组成部分,这种方法有效地减轻了灾难性的遗忘. 此外,CLG-CBM[59]纳入了语言指导概念瓶颈模式。 为了保持任务之间的语义一致性,这些模型使视觉特征与人可解释的概念空间一致. MG-CLIP [27] 引入了模式漏洞保全和补偿,以减轻遗忘和改进适应新任务的情况,而HERMAN [60]则为基于CLIP的CIL提出了等级代表比对. 然而,现有的基于CLIP的CIL方法仍然主要依靠全球表示来进行递增识别,使得CLIP内部的补丁级视觉特征和符号级文字语义没有得到充分的探索. 本文旨在探讨长期被忽视的《国际劳工法典》中的当地代表,以提高《国际劳工法典》的逐步认可程度。

blocks.en: III Preliminaries
blocks.zh: 三. 初步情况

blocks.en: In this section, we introduce the background information of CIL and provide an overview of the CLIP model. Finally, we discuss the typical approaches for CLIP-based CIL.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们介绍该中心的背景资料,并概述该中心的模式。 最后,我们讨论以《刑法》为基础的《刑法》的典型做法。

blocks.en: III-A Class-Incremental Learning
blocks.zh: 三级A级强化学习

blocks.en: Class-Incremental Learning (CIL) aims to construct a unified classifier capable of recognizing all seen classes from a sequential data stream [ 4 ] , [ 61 ] . Consider a training sequence consisting of B B tasks, denoted as { 𝒟 1 , 𝒟 2 , ⋯ , 𝒟 B } \left\{\mathcal{D}^{1},\mathcal{D}^{2},\cdots,\mathcal{D}^{B}\right\} , where each task 𝒟 b = { ( 𝐱 i , y i ) } i = 1 n b \mathcal{D}^{b}=\left\{\left(\mathbf{x}_{i},y_{i}\right)\right\}_{i=1}^{n_{b}} contains n b n_{b} examples. Here, 𝐱 i ∈ ℝ D \mathbf{x}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{D} is an instance of class y i ∈ Y b y_{i}\in Y_{b} , and Y b Y_{b} denotes the label space corresponding to task b b . The label spaces from different tasks are mutually disjoint ( i.e. , Y b ∩ Y b ′ = ∅ Y_{b}\cap Y_{b^{\prime}}=\varnothing for b ≠ b ′ b\neq b^{\prime} ). Under the exemplar-free setting [ 54 ] , [ 62 ] , the model is prohibited from accessing any historical samples from task 𝒟 1 : b − 1 \mathcal{D}^{1:b-1} when adapting to the new task 𝒟 b \mathcal{D}^{b} . The objective of CIL is to construct a unified classifier for all seen classes 𝒴 b = Y 1 ∪ ⋯ ∪ Y b \mathcal{Y}_{b}=Y_{1}\cup\cdots\cup Y_{b} . Given an input image 𝐱 ∈ ℝ D \mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{R}^{D} , the image encoder g i ​ ( ⋅ ) g_{i}(\cdot) ( e.g. , Vision Transformer) first splits it into M M fixed-size patches. blocks.en: To fully leverage the rich local information contained within CLIP, enabling the model to adapt to downstream tasks and prevent forgetting, we propose PACE . In Sec. IV-A , we first extract the top- k k most discriminative local features from the visual patch-level and textual token-level sequences. We map the features of each modality to an independent shared space to enhance adaptability in downstream tasks. Subsequently, in Sec. IV-B , we design a cross-modal fusion module that uses global features as queries to aggregate cross-modal local features, thereby explicitly injecting local knowledge into the global representations. To mitigate catastrophic forgetting, we leverage a subspace projection-based parameter update strategy to protect the critical weight subspaces associated with local feature utilization in Sec. IV-C . Lastly, Sec. IV-D provides a summary of PACE and outlines the detailed guidelines for training and inference.

blocks.en: After extracting the most discriminative local features in 𝒱 ^ \hat{\mathcal{V}} and 𝒯 ^ i \hat{\mathcal{T}}^{i} in Sec. IV-A , these rich local details remain isolated from the global decision-making embeddings ( i.e. , v cls \textbf{v}_{\text{cls}} and t eos i \textbf{t}_{\text{eos}}^{i} ) used for final classification, making it difficult to fully realize the discriminative potential of the local information. To address this issue, we introduce the cross-modal fusion module to leverage local features ( 𝒱 ^ \hat{\mathcal{V}} or 𝒯 ^ i \hat{\mathcal{T}}^{i} ) to enhance the global representation ( v cls \textbf{v}_{\text{cls}} or t eos i \textbf{t}_{\text{eos}}^{i} ) of the other modality. Specifically, the global representation of one modality acts as the query, aiming to enhance the cross-modal semantic representation capability of that global feature by selectively attending to the local feature sequence of the other modality (serving as the key and value). This mechanism establishes two semantic fusion branches, which we detail below.

Task-Specific Projector. Despite the enhanced classification capability provided by the cross-modal fusion module, we observed that the model requires specific adaptation for various downstream tasks. To effectively adapt the model to downstream tasks while preserving its generalization ability, we introduce two task-specific linear projectors, which consist of a task-specific visual projector M v ​ ( ⋅ ) : ℝ d → ℝ d \textbf{M}_{v}(\cdot):\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d} and a textual projector M t ​ ( ⋅ ) : ℝ d → ℝ d \textbf{M}_{t}(\cdot):\mathbb{R}^{d}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}^{d} . These projectors are placed immediately after the top- k k local features selection for each incremental task b b . To prevent catastrophic forgetting during update, we instantiate new task-specific modules M v b \textbf{M}_{v}^{b} and M t b \textbf{M}_{t}^{b} during the training of task b b . Simultaneously, we freeze the parameters of all historical modules { M v 1 : b − 1 , M t 1 : b − 1 } \{\textbf{M}_{v}^{1:b-1},\textbf{M}_{t}^{1:b-1}\} to preserve the learned representations of previous classes. Finally, we cumulatively aggregate the outputs from all frozen and active projectors. The projected visual feature v ~ cls \tilde{\textbf{v}}_{\text{cls}} and textual feature t ~ eos i \tilde{\textbf{t}}_{\text{eos}}^{i} are computed as: v ~ cls \displaystyle\tilde{\textbf{v}}_{\text{cls}} = 𝐌 v b ​ ( v cls ) + ∑ i = 1 b − 1 𝐌 ¯ v i ​ ( v cls ) , \displaystyle={\mathbf{M}}_{v}^{b}(\textbf{v}_{\text{cls}})+\sum_{i=1}^{b-1}\bar{\mathbf{M}}_{v}^{i}(\textbf{v}_{\text{cls}}), (18) t ~ eos i \displaystyle\tilde{\textbf{t}}_{\text{eos}}^{i} = 𝐌 t b ​ ( t eos i ) + ∑ i = 1 b − 1 𝐌 ¯ t i ​ ( t eos i ) , \displaystyle={\mathbf{M}}_{t}^{b}(\textbf{t}_{\text{eos}}^{i})+\sum_{i=1}^{b-1}\bar{\mathbf{M}}_{t}^{i}(\textbf{t}_{\text{eos}}^{i}), (19) where 𝐌 ¯ v i ​ ( ⋅ ) \bar{\mathbf{M}}_{v}^{i}(\cdot) and 𝐌 ¯ t i ​ ( ⋅ ) \bar{\mathbf{M}}_{t}^{i}(\cdot) denote the frozen projectors corresponding to the visual and textual modalities in the i i -th incremental task, respectively.
Eq. 18 and Eq. 19 ensure that the model remains stable and adapts efficiently to new tasks, without forgetting previously learned knowledge. So we use the cumulatively aggregated features ( i.e. , v ~ cls , t ~ eos i , 𝒱 ~ \tilde{\textbf{v}}_{\text{cls}},\tilde{\textbf{t}}_{\text{eos}}^{i},\tilde{\mathcal{V}} and 𝒯 ~ i \tilde{\mathcal{T}}^{i} ) from the task-specific projectors to replace
the raw features ( i.e. , v cls , t eos i , 𝒱 ^ \textbf{v}_{\text{cls}},\textbf{t}_{\text{eos}}^{i},\hat{\mathcal{V}} and 𝒯 ^ i \hat{\mathcal{T}}^{i} ) originally fed into the cross-modal fusion module in Eq. 9 and Eq. 10 . blocks.en: Within the cross-modal fusion module, the weight matrices { W Q \{\textbf{W}^{Q} , W K \textbf{W}^{K} , W V } \textbf{W}^{V}\} are globally shared. Across incremental tasks, this shared structure is highly susceptible to catastrophic forgetting. Therefore, we employ a parameter update strategy based on subspace projection to preserve the critical local knowledge subspace of previous tasks.

Pseudo Code. We give the pseudo-code of PACE to illustrate
the training process in Algorithm 1 . At each incremental stage b b , the model takes the current task dataset 𝒟 b \mathcal{D}^{b} together with the previous subspace projection matrix 𝐏 old \mathbf{P}_{\text{old}} as input. Before optimization, all projectors learned from previous tasks are frozen (Line 1 ), while new visual and textual projectors are initialized for the current task (Line 2 ). During training, for each instance-label pair, we first extract the visual and textual features using the frozen CLIP encoders (Line 4 to Line 5 ), and then apply the patch-token information selection module to select the top- k k discriminative visual patches and textual tokens (Line 6 ). Based on these selected features, we compute the projected representations and perform cross-modal fusion to enhance both global and local features (Line 7 to Line 8 ). The logits are then obtained for model optimization (Line 9 ), followed by loss computation and parameter updating (Line 10 ). After finishing the current task b b , we further correct the shared fusion weights via subspace projection when b > 1 b>1 , and update the projection matrix 𝐏 old \mathbf{P}_{\text{old}} for the next incremental stage (Line 12 to Line 15 ). The final updated model is then returned as the output of the training process.

blocks.en: Dataset. Following [ 20 ] , [ 62 ] , we evaluate our method on nine benchmark datasets, i.e. , CIFAR100 [ 66 ] , CUB200 [ 67 ] , ObjectNet [ 68 ] , ImageNet-R [ 69 ] , FGVCAircraft [ 70 ] , StanfordCars [ 71 ] , Food101 [ 72 ] , SUN397 [ 73 ] and UCF101 [ 74 ] . For data splitting, we adopt the sampling strategy of [ 20 ] , sampling 100 classes from CIFAR100, Aircraft, Cars, Food, UCF, 200 classes from CUB200, ObjectNet, ImageNet-R, and 300 classes from SUN. Dataset split. Following [ 4 ] , [ 53 ] , we utilize ‘B- m m Inc- n n ’ to split the classes in CIL. Here, m m denotes the number of classes in the initial stage, while n n represents the number of classes in each subsequent incremental stage. For fair comparison, following [ 4 ] , we randomly shuffle the class order using a random seed of 1993 and use the same order for all methods. Comparison methods. We first compare the performance against current SOTA CIL methods based on pre-trained models, e.g. , L2P [ 53 ] , DualPrompt [ 54 ] , CODA-Prompt [ 51 ] , and SimpleCIL [ 65 ] . Furthermore, we compare with SOTA CLIP-based CIL methods, e.g. , CoOp [ 62 ] , RAPF [ 58 ] , CLG-CBM [ 59 ] , MG-CLIP [ 27 ] , HERMAN [ 60 ] , and PROOF [ 20 ] . We use the finetune approach as a sequential fine-tuning baseline and adopt ZS-CLIP [ 15 ] as a reference for CLIP on downstream tasks. All compared methods are initialized using the same CLIP weights. Training details. Our experiments are implemented in PyTorch 2.0.1 based on the C3Box [ 75 ] toolbox. To ensure a fair comparison, all compared methods are based on the CLIP with ViT-B/16 backbone, following [ 20 ] , [ 58 ] . For vision-based methods that cannot leverage the textual prompt ( e.g. , L2P, DualPrompt, CODA-Prompt), we initialize them using CLIP’s visual branch. Our method is optimized using SGD with a batch size of 64 over 10 epochs. The initial learning rate is set to 0.05 and is decayed via a cosine annealing scheduler. We set the energy threshold γ \gamma for orthogonal projection to 0.9, the subspace weighting factor α \alpha to 0.9, the local feature selection size k k to 8, and the balance coefficient λ \lambda to 0.15. Detailed analyses of these important hyperparameters are provided in Sec. V-C . Our experimental results are based on the LAION-400M pre-trained CLIP model [ 76 ] . Evaluation metric. Following [ 4 ] , [ 20 ] , we let 𝒜 b \mathcal{A}_{b} represent the model’s accuracy after the b b -th incremental stage. We use two main metrics to evaluate our method: the last accuracy 𝒜 B \mathcal{A}_{B} , which measures performance after the last task, and the average accuracy 𝒜 ¯ = 1 B ​ ∑ b = 1 B 𝒜 b \bar{\mathcal{A}}=\frac{1}{B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\mathcal{A}_{b} , which represents the mean accuracy across all stages.

blocks.en: We benchmark PACE against SOTA methods on nine benchmark datasets and report the results in Tab. I and Fig. 2 . Specifically, PACE consistently achieves superior performance. The Finetune baseline consistently performs the worst among all compared methods. Furthermore, we observe that visual prompt-based methods, such as L2P, DualPrompt, and CODA-Prompt, encounter performance ceilings primarily because they fail to leverage the rich textual semantics. Similarly, the textual prompt-tuning method CoOp suffers from prompt forgetting across tasks, resulting in degraded performance. Notably, PACE outperforms other CLIP-based CIL methods, such as RAPF, further demonstrating its effectiveness in leveraging multimodal information and robustly mitigating catastrophic forgetting. This substantial advantage is attributed to our strategy of effectively leveraging critical localized information. Our cross-modal fusion module is specifically designed to achieve stronger cross-modal alignment by integrating information from visual patch tokens with token-level textual descriptors, thereby enabling a more robust and contextually aware representation for incremental tasks.

Ablation study. We conduct detailed ablations on Cars B0 Inc10 to investigate the contribution of the core components of PACE , with results presented in Fig. 3(a) . PACE consistently maintains the highest accuracy across all incremental stages, demonstrating a widening performance gap over the baseline as the number of classes increases. Specifically, the ZS-CLIP baseline performs worst, and the removal of the cross-modal fusion denoted as ‘w/o Fusion’ ( i.e. , not using Eq. 12 and Eq. 16 ), results in a substantial and sustained performance drop, confirming the necessity of explicitly fusing discriminative patch-level visual features and token-level textual semantics to maintain high classification power in CIL. Conversely, the removal of the local knowledge preservation mechanism, denoted as ‘w/o Subspace Projection’ ( i.e. , removing Eq. 24 ), shows a milder impact in early stages but incurs a rapid decline in later stages as interference from new tasks accumulates. This result highlights
the vital role of the subspace projection strategy in stabilizing prior knowledge and effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting.

blocks.en: Trainable parameters. We further report the detailed number of trainable parameters for each compared method in Fig. 3(b) . As shown in the figure, PACE maintains a scale of trainable parameters comparable to other competitive methods. Specifically, we only update the task-specific parameters within the current task’s projector, while keeping the parameters corresponding to all previous tasks frozen. Furthermore, the parameters of the cross-modal fusion module are globally shared throughout the entire continual learning sequence. This design allows PACE to mitigate parameter expansion across sequential tasks while achieving superior performance.

blocks.en: Computational Overhead Analysis. We further compare the computational overhead of different CIL methods on Cars B0 Inc10. As shown in Table IV , PACE achieves the highest average accuracy while maintaining moderate computational overhead. The patch-token information selection only requires affinity computation between global and patch-level features followed by lightweight top- k k selection. The cross-modal enhancement performs interactions only on selected tokens instead of the complete token sequences, while task-specific projectors introduce only lightweight linear projections during inference. Overall, PACE achieves a favorable trade-off between recognition performance and computational efficiency.

blocks.en: V-D Extending PACE with LLM-Generated Descriptions
blocks.zh: V-D 扩展带 LLM- Generated 描述的 PACE

blocks.en: To further investigate the capability of PACE to exploit richer token-level textual semantics, we extend the original fixed prompt with LLM-generated class-specific visual descriptions and construct PACE ++. Specifically, we employ GPT-5.4 to generate discriminative visual descriptions for each class. For a class y i y_{i} , we provide its class name as the input to GPT-5.4 [ 78 ] with the following prompt: Q : What are the key visual features for identifying a [CLASS] i in a photo? Focus on the most discriminative attributes. A : 1. Pointed triangular ears. 2. Vertical-slit pupils. 3. ⋯ \cdots Based on this instruction, GPT-5.4 generates a set of class-specific visual descriptions containing discriminative attributes, such as shape, color, and local structures. These generated descriptions are then used to replace the original fixed prompt “A photo of a [CLASS]” and fed into the frozen CLIP text encoder to obtain the corresponding token-level textual features 𝐓 i \mathbf{T}^{i} . Compared with PACE , PACE ++ only modifies the textual prompt construction process by replacing the fixed template with LLM-generated visual descriptions. The frozen CLIP text encoder, subsequent token selection, and cross-modal enhancement module remain unchanged. We further evaluate PACE ++ on nine benchmark datasets to investigate the effectiveness of richer textual descriptions. As shown in Table I , PACE ++ achieves comparable overall performance and obtains improvements on several datasets compared with PACE , indicating that the generated visual descriptions can provide additional semantic information for local token alignment.

blocks.en: VI Conclusion
blocks.zh: 六 结论

blocks.en: Class-incremental learning is crucial for real-world applications. The PACE method proposed in this paper aims to enhance CLIP’s CIL capabilities by leveraging the rich patch-level visual features and token-level textual semantics that have largely been underutilized in CLIP. Specifically, we extract top- k k discriminative local features and subsequently use cross-modal fusion to leverage this local information to enhance global representations and alignment. Furthermore, a subspace-based knowledge preservation strategy effectively mitigates catastrophic forgetting in the shared fusion module. Extensive experiments validate PACE ’s superior performance.
blocks.zh: 课堂增量学习对现实世界的应用至关重要. 本文中提议的PACE方法旨在通过利用CLIP中基本未充分利用的丰富的补丁级视觉特征和符号级文字语义来增强CLIP的CIL能力. 具体地说,我们提取了顶级-k k 的歧视性本地特征,然后利用跨模式聚变来利用这种本地信息,增强全球代表性和一致性。 此外,基于空间的亚知识保存战略有效地减轻了共享聚变模块中发生的灾难性遗忘。 广泛的实验验证了PACE的优异性能.

blocks.en: Limitations and Future Work. Our current framework utilizes a fixed prompt for the textual branch, which may limit the model’s ability to capture semantic diversity and fully exploit the power of the vision-language model in specific CIL scenarios. In the future, we will explore a richer prompt engineering strategy to further enhance textual representation and cross-modal alignment capability, e.g. , learnable prompts.
blocks.zh: 限制和今后的工作。 我们目前的框架对文字分支使用固定的提示,这可能会限制该模型掌握语义多样性的能力,并在具体的CIL情景中充分利用视觉语言模型的力量。 今后,我们将探索一项更丰富的即时工程战略,以进一步加强文字代表性和跨模式对齐能力,例如可学习的诱因。
